cr-impact.assumptions: The request is a to-do list: anybody adds a task, marks it done, and possibly edits or deletes it. It is persisted on the server, because system-states.md says the browser stores nothing. cr-requirements and cr-scenarios will take impact.md as today's state and will turn its "could not determine" list into questions. That list covers: keep or replace the guestbook; whether "odznaczenie" means a done task can be unticked; whether "ew." makes edit/delete optional; what fields a task has; seed data; the route and the `/` redirect; and simultaneous toggles.

cr-requirements.assumptions: What I assume scenarios.md will do: Every one of R-1 to R-10 gets at least one scenario. Screen-only clauses get their proof from the frontend suite, because the black box speaks HTTP. These are R-1 cl.1, R-3.6, R-4 cl.5-6, R-5, the R-7 confirmation, and R-10. R-9 scenarios send both changes before either one is answered. Values are used as written: 200/201 code points, 200xU+1F600, 200x(U+0065 U+0301), 2+200+2 as typed and 205 spaces, 101 tasks, and at least 3 example tasks each under 150 code points. R-11 is manual, so it needs a numbered step in uat.md. No scenario asserts D1, D2 or D3 behaviour until the user decides them.

cr-scenarios.assumptions: I took requirements.md as the authority. The user answered Q-10, Q-11 and Q-12 after it was written, and it still lists them as the open questions D1, D2 and D3. I wrote seeds for those answers (S-8, S-9, the last row of S-33, S-49, S-52, S-53) under the requirement each one would amend, and flagged each of them (finding 8). The coherence round has to amend R-2 and R-11, or those seeds prove clauses nobody wrote. Every boundary I used is stated in the requirements, apart from S-9 (a line break at the end of a task is trimmed), which I read from Q-11's word "inside" together with R-2 clause 1 and flagged.
